meta.purpose: A dedicated review section. Each suggestion is a proposal with a stated benefit, cost, risk of adopting it, and a status. The owner reviews and chooses the path BEFORE anything is implemented. Nothing on this page has been auto-applied.
meta.how_to_use: Read the suggested path first, then the individual proposals. Each proposal carries a 'decision needed from you' line so a choice can be recorded. Statuses are: proposed, under review, rejected, adopted. None are adopted.

suggested_path.name: Path A — Close the cheap gaps first, then decide
suggested_path.rationale: Two of the fifteen gaps cost nothing and take days: the Census API key (G-02) and the decline-in-value filing whose window closes 2026-11-30. A third, the lease date (G-04), is already in the owner's filing cabinet. Those three move the project further than any additional research, because they turn an eight-year uncertainty into a date and turn city averages into tract figures.
steps: Register a Census API key and re-run the documented tract query. (free, under an hour of work)
Pull the executed lease and write down four dates: option window opens, option deadline, tenant notice date, expiration. (free)
If assessed value exceeds market value, file the decline-in-value application before 2026-11-30. (free, dated)
Read the insurance binder and record premium, limits, deductibles, BI period and renewal date. (free)
Only then engage brokers for cap-rate opinions and order a property condition and seismic assessment. (paid, but now scoped to the right asset and term)
suggested_path.why_not_alternative: Path B (start with brokers and diligence) spends money before the term is even known. Pricing a 3-year asset and a 9-year asset are different exercises; doing the expensive work first risks having to redo it.
suggested_path.decision_needed_from_you: Approve Path A, or choose Path B, or write your own order on the Flagged for Review page.

paths.name: Path A — cheap gaps first, then decide
paths.main_risk: The lease date turns out to be 2035, in which case there was less urgency than assumed — a good problem.

paths.name: Path B — engage brokers and diligence immediately
paths.cost: Property condition assessment plus appraisal plus broker opinions
paths.speed_to_first_real_answer: Four to six weeks, at higher cost
paths.main_risk: Diligence scoped before the remaining term is known may need redoing.

paths.name: Path C — sell now on the belief that rates and lease term are both against the owner
paths.main_risk: Irreversible. The gain is taxed at California ordinary-income rates and 25% recapture, and the §1031 clock starts on closing. Selling before reading the renewal option can also forfeit a valuable right.

paths.name: Path D — hold and do nothing until 2030
paths.cost: Deferred maintenance and unpriced insurance repricing
paths.main_risk: Insurance and capex risk accrue silently, and the option window could be missed entirely.

proposals.proposal: Keep the site working without the address by making every 'unverified' state visible rather than hidden.
proposals.benefit: A reader can never mistake a reference-point figure for the parcel's figure. The site stays usable while remaining honest.
proposals.risk: The dashboard looks emptier than a confident-looking competitor page. That is the point.
proposals.decision_needed: Confirm you want visible blanks rather than plausible-looking estimates.

proposals.proposal: Ship the calculator as a browser-only tool that never transmits inputs.
proposals.benefit: Rent, basis, tax brackets and financing can all be modelled without any private data leaving the owner's machine or entering this repository.
proposals.risk: Nothing persists between visits; the reader must re-enter inputs.
proposals.decision_needed: Accept the no-persistence trade-off, or request an export-to-file option instead.

proposals.proposal: Add a printable one-page advisor brief that contains no private figures.
proposals.benefit: An adviser can be briefed in a single page without exposing the owner's finances on a website.
proposals.risk: The one-pager must be regenerated whenever the underlying data changes.

proposals.proposal: Treat the metro back-test result — strong mean reversion in 5-year appreciation — as the reason to model zero real appreciation by default.
proposals.benefit: Prevents the most common error in this asset class: underwriting the last five years' growth forever.
proposals.risk: If the regime has genuinely changed, the default is too conservative. The calculator lets the reader override it.
proposals.decision_needed: Accept zero real appreciation as the default, or set your own growth assumption.

proposals.proposal: Model the compound hazard case (damage + rent loss + no buyers) as the primary stress, rather than three separate shocks.
proposals.benefit: Reflects the actual mechanism that destroys an individual owner's wealth: forced sale into a dead market.
proposals.risk: Qualitative only until insurance and condition documents arrive.
proposals.decision_needed: Confirm the compound framing matches how you think about your exposure.

proposals.proposal: Consider §1031 before listing, not after closing.
proposals.benefit: It is the only structural lever that changes the after-tax result without changing the price, and it cannot be elected retroactively.
proposals.risk: The 45-day identification is tight and can force a rushed replacement purchase — the reason MT-06 says to pre-identify candidates.
proposals.decision_needed: Decide whether a replacement property strategy exists, before any listing.

proposals.proposal: Pin the renewal-notice dates even if you intend to sell.
proposals.benefit: A live, unexpired option is a saleable feature; a lapsed one is not. This is the only irreversible item in the whole project.
proposals.decision_needed: Confirm the dates are now recorded in the private calendar.

proposals.proposal: Buy or build a proper 1/3/5-mile ring analysis instead of relying on city averages.
proposals.benefit: Directly closes the owner's W-01 requirement. City-level income and population genuinely cannot substitute.
proposals.cost: Free if built from Census tract data with a documented weighting method; paid if bought from a vendor
proposals.risk: Vendor data is not official and would have to be labelled as non-official on the site.

proposals.proposal: Add a quarterly data-refresh calendar pinned to release schedules rather than arbitrary dates.
proposals.benefit: The unverified flags clear predictably; stale figures get caught.
proposals.decision_needed: Confirm you want a recurring refresh, or a one-time snapshot.

proposals.proposal: Adopt the Flagged for Review page as the permanent change-request queue.
proposals.benefit: Every unverified item and irregularity has a permalink and a source, so a decision can be recorded against it rather than lost in email.
proposals.decision_needed: Confirm this becomes the canonical review queue.

proposals.proposal: Resist the temptation to add a 'recommended' badge to any scenario until G-04 and G-06 close.
proposals.benefit: Protects against a confident-looking answer that is really an invented cap rate plus an eight-year date window.
proposals.cost: The dashboard has no headline verdict.
proposals.risk: Stakeholders often want a one-word answer. The honest one-word answer today is 'not yet'.
proposals.decision_needed: Accept 'not yet' as the current deliverable, or tell me which input you can supply first so it can change.

proposals.benefit: Reduces the property tax line — the biggest fixed expense in a NNN hold — for the 2026-2027 tax year. Free to file.
proposals.risk: Requires assessed value to exceed market value; the county page publishes the window and deadline, but eligibility depends on the parcel's actual assessment.
proposals.decision_needed: Check the assessed value and file if eligible. This is time-critical.

review_workflow.action: Owner reads Path A through D and marks one as chosen (or writes a custom order).
Owner goes through SG-01 to SG-12 and sets each to under review, rejected or adopted.
Only adopted items get implemented, in a separate commit, with the decision recorded in COORDINATION.md.
Anything still unverified stays on the Flagged for Review page regardless of adoption.
